text: The Patriots delivered one of the week's most genuinely impressive results by knocking off the Bills 29-26 at Highmark Stadium—a victory that became particularly meaningful as New England became the first team to win in Buffalo's new facility, and one that coach Mike Vrabel deemed critical for the defending AFC East champions. Drake Maye, who had struggled early in the season, orchestrated a game-winning drive and overcame two turnovers by throwing three touchdown passes, proving he didn't need a perfect performance to get the job done against Josh Allen and company. The win naturally sparked considerable speculation about whether the Patriots are genuinely back on track for another division title or whether we're all getting ahead of ourselves with Week 4 overreactions, though the health report on the roster—with all six of the team's questionable players, including Dre'Mont Jones, Craig Woodson, and Eli Raridon, returning to active status for the matchup—certainly helped the cause. This was the kind of road statement win that separates contenders from pretenders, and Mike Reiss's analysis of how the Patriots pulled it off at a rival's new house suggests there's more substance here than simple Week 4 noise.
